question: Whether WinINet's capture keeps a request the server answers with a redirect, which WinINet follows by itself, as one exchange or as two - and what it keeps of each: the request redirected and the redirect, then the request WinINet makes to the location and its answer.
answer: As two, each an exchange of its own: the request the server redirected and its redirect - a head and an empty body, whole - under one exchange number, and the request WinINet made to the location and its answer under another, numbered apart (3 to 15 later, eight clients at once) and begun once the redirect's response had ended, every time. No record ties the two. Every part of both legs matched the server's truth. After a POST answered 301, 302 or 303, WinINet asked the location with GET and no body; after 307 or 308 it failed the send with ERROR_HTTP_REDIRECT_NEEDS_CONFIRMATION (12168) until its client confirmed the redirect by sending the request again, when it made the same POST, body and all, to the location. Nothing was lost.

probe.tool: tools/InterCat.WinInetProbe --redirect 301|302|303|307|308 [--tls] [--async] [--concurrency 8 --requests 64 --ledger], 16 requests each or 64 eight at once, beside a decoy outside the process filter; the server answers each request first with the redirect, of no body, to its path moved, and logs each leg apart; the client confirms a redirect WinINet asks it to by sending its request again

runs.run: 307 Temporary Redirect, confirmed by the client
308 Permanent Redirect, confirmed by the client
302, eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept
307, eight at once, its buffers' metadata kept

capture.command: icat record --profile content --source etw/manifest/Microsoft-Windows-WinINet-Capture --mechanism http --pid <workload> --channel * --max-record-bytes 65536 --max-session-bytes 67108864 --inspection hex-text --duration 25, beside InterCat.TestWorkloads http-wininet --requests 64 --start-after 8 --redirect 302|307 --concurrency 8; then icat exchanges --exchanges 10000 --decode, and each part of each exchange saved by icat content --part and matched by SHA-256 with the server's truth of its leg

runs.run: 307, eight at once, each redirect confirmed by the client

ledger: fixtures/FX-HTTP-009/evidence/302-eight-at-once/buffers.csv and 307-eight-at-once/buffers.csv: each buffer the probe captured of its 64 requests' 128 exchanges, in time order - its 100 ns readings after the first, event, exchange number, place, ends, length, the request its exchange's head named, whether a thread that made a request raised it, and its leg: the one the server redirected, or the one to the path moved - never its bytes. A test groups each as a session's records are grouped, rebuilds each head from the scenario and checks it against the server's truth byte for byte, and holds each redirect to its own request there.
note: A redirect's response body is empty, and kept as one buffer of no byte, whole by its ends; a GET to the location has no body, and no record is raised for one, as for request 0's empty body in either leg. WinINet's own GET keeps the request's fields but Content-Length, in their order; a POST its client sent again takes the client's added field anew, after WinINet's own. Neither the truth nor this file holds a byte of what was sent or read.
